column1: # Old jupiterlaser.com URL -> its closest equivalent on the new site.
# Source of truth. _dev/gen-redirects.py writes vercel.json, _redirects and
# .htaccess from this file, so the three can never drift apart. Edit here, then
# run the generator. Do not hand-edit the three outputs.
# Built from a real crawl of all four Yoast sitemaps (_dev/crawl-old-site.py),
# not from guessing slugs: 157 live URLs, of which 8 already exist unchanged on
# the new site and 149 need a target. Before this, 27 redirects covered 17 of
# them and 132 URLs would have 404'd the moment DNS moved.
# The rule that matters: redirect to the closest *equivalent*, never to / in
# bulk. Google treats a mass redirect to the homepage as a soft 404 and discards
# the link equity, which is the whole thing a redirect exists to carry. Nothing
# in this file targets /. Where no specific page exists, the section hub is the
# honest answer -- a reader landing on /conditions/ from a hammer-toe article
# has somewhere to go; one landing on / does not.
# Columns: old path (no trailing slash) <TAB> destination <TAB> why
# ---- Pages: services and conditions the old site had as top-level -----------
